Title: Build and own your software factory : Mastra Discussion Forums | Product Hunt
Build AI agents with a modern TypeScript stack. # Build and own your software factory. @Mastra launched an open-source, configurable software factory this month. Ranked #1 Product of the Day and #1 Product of the Week, the community loved it. To keep the conversation going, @bookercodes and @suhdudeitsabhi are hosting a workshop this Thursday, September 17, at 4 PM UTC / 9 AM PST. ​In this workshop, @bookercodes and @suhdudeitsabhi will build a Factory, connect it to a real repository, and show how agents move an issue from initial investigation to a reviewed pull request. They'll also take you inside Shipyard, their own software factory. Over one three-week period, Shipyard authored more than a quarter of the pull requests merged into @Mastra. They'll explain how they use it to ship an open-source project, including handling repository issues, reviewing contributions, and coordinating work across the team. ## What's inside. * ​Setting up and owning an open-source Factory, including models, authentication, storage, sandboxes, and deployment. * ​Bringing work in from GitHub, Linear, and Slack, then moving it through investigation, planning, building, and review. * ​Configuring stages with specialized agents, skills, rules, and workflows, including alternative coding harnesses through ACP. * ​Following and steering shared agent sessions, preserving implementation context, and running pull request review in a separate linked session. **​Join the live demo:** **luma.com/mastra**. ### Replies. Congrats on the #1 Product of the Day *and* Week that's a strong signal the "configurable software factory" framing actually resonated, not just launch-day novelty. Curious going in, is the workshop more aimed at people evaluating whether to adopt it, or hands-on for folks already building with it? Trying to figure out how deep to go on setup beforehand versus just showing up and following along.

A desktop app for Git branches and GitHub pull requests. Comment on any line, publish when you're ready, and add an AI reviewer with your own model, or none. Since AI started writing so much of our code, reviewing it all has become the hardest part of my job. So I built Review: a desktop app for reviewing pull requests, where you can set up a team of AI reviewers from different providers to take the first pass. - Opens your local Git branches and GitHub pull requests in one window. - Keeps your comments on your machine until you publish them to GitHub as a review. **What's different about the AI part**: it checks every change against a fixed set of rules (bugs, security, error handling, tests and more), and it shows which rules it actually checked, not just what it found. If a request fails, you can retry only the rules it missed. One heads-up: the installers aren't signed yet, so your system will ask once the first time you open it. I'd love to know: what's the most annoying part of code review for you today? No reviews yet Be the first to leave a review for Review Leave a review.
